reasons.A: Closest movement: short plain declaratives mostly in first person with occasional 'you', 'So I start...' openings and flat understatement ('I keep it. I do not use it much.') without overdoing the fragments.
reasons.D: Right clipped rhythm and plain diction, but leans harder on imperatives and chops sentences more thickly than the passage ('It feels slower. It is not.'), tipping towards caricature.
reasons.B: Short sentences and plain stance fit, but more rhetorical emphasis ('This is the big one', 'or rather', 'This matters more than you think') and list-like fragments give a chattier, more persuasive tone than the author.
reasons.C: Long, smoothly subordinated sentences, a colon and a polished advice-column register; the opposite of the author's terse, concrete, first-person movement.
